articles.title: MapQuest is now the No. 1 US app after bucking Trump's 'Lake America' renaming | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The once-dominant mapping app has surged to the top of Apple’s U.S. App Store after refusing to adopt Trump’s “Lake America” name, drawing more than half of its 2026 U.S. downloads in just six days.
articles.body_text: MapQuest’s unlikely comeback just got even bigger. On Tuesday, the “OG” mapping application (and one that many thought no longer existed!) became the No. 1 overall app on the U.S. App Store, up from No. 8 on Monday . The surge in new downloads was inspired by MapQuest’s refusal to rename Lake Ontario as “Lake America,” after President Trump’s executive order directed the U.S. geographic naming service to adopt the new name amid his ongoing trade push. After the August 27 order, MapQuest announced on X that it would not change the lake’s name, while both Google Maps and, later, Apple Maps , capitulated. As a result, MapQuest’s U.S. App Store ranking steadily climbed, as consumers downloaded the app to show their support for the company’s stance. The people have spoken. We are working. pic.twitter.com/WeO7OAJ2T7 MapQuest’s rank climbed from No. 128 on August 28 to No. 92 the following day, and then hit No. 3 this Monday, August 31, when it was also No. 1 in the Navigation category . By Tuesday of this week, MapQuest had reached the No. 1 spot across both apps and games on the U.S. App Store. Since the executive order was issued, the app has been downloaded an estimated 632,000 times in the U.S., according to data from market intelligence provider Sensor Tower. Reached for comment, MapQuest said the app had actually seen over 1.5 million installs across the U.S. and Canada combined. MapQuest also said many of these new users aren’t just casual downloaders; they’re actively engaging with the app. “What’s been incredible is that people aren’t just installing our app — they care enough to communicate directly with us — making feature requests and submitting bug reports on social, and in our app reviews,” MapQuest GM Doug Berger told TechCrunch via email. “Our small team has been working around the clock to build features people are asking for. We are aiming for everyone to have a great experience with the app,” he said. The surge has come quickly for the company. More than half of MapQuest’s year-to-date U.S. downloads —56% — have occurred from August 27 through September 1, Sensor Tower’s estimates show. During this time period, the app’s U.S. downloads increased by 123% day-over-day and were up more than 50 times compared to the same period last year, its data indicates. Part of what made MapQuest’s stance resonate with consumers was its contrast with its much larger Big Tech rivals. Google last week explained its decision to rename the lake, saying that it updates names to reflect changes in official government sources such as the Geographic Names Information System (GNIS) in the U.S. Apple didn’t provide a comment , but likely follows the same guidelines. As a much smaller player, MapQuest has more freedom to take a stand and buck the typical conventions.

articles.summary: An identity theft search site claimed to have more than 150 million driver's license photos stolen from an ID verification service. The crime site has now shut down.
articles.body_text: If you have handed over your driver’s license, passport, or other form of identity document to verify your information in the real world, like at a bar, a weed store, or when booking a car rental, there’s a good chance it’s now been stolen in a suspected massive data breach. That’s according to a jaw-dropping report by independent security journalist Brian Krebs, who says a company used to verify government-issued identity documents in the real world was likely hacked and its vast stores of people’s ID cards were exfiltrated. Krebs reports that an identity theft site called Nexus, which launched on the dark web this week, claimed to allow users to search through more than 150 million driver’s licenses and passports belonging to people who live in the United States and Canada. A post advertising the site on a known Russian cybercrime forum said Nexus added about half a million new documents daily, sourced from a “major identity verification company,” implying that the hackers had near real-time access to the identity verification company’s systems. The advert claims that “customer photos are displayed if available.” Krebs found that his own driver’s license was among the searchable records in the database, confirming that the data was authentic. Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth was also among the people whose photos were listed on the identity search site. A spokesperson for the Department of Defense told TechCrunch that it is “aware of these reports and is evaluating them.” Working with security researcher Zach Edwards , whose ID card was also stolen in the breach, Krebs identified the likely source as the identity verification service IDScan . The Louisiana-based company is relied on by major tech and consumer brands to verify tens of millions of people’s IDs around the world each month. IDScan chief executive Jimmy Roussel did not return TechCrunch’s request for comment, but the company’s chief operating officer Jillian Kossman told Krebs that the company was investigating. Krebs said the FBI’s field office in New Orleans is also probing the breach. A spokesperson for the FBI did not respond to TechCrunch’s inquiry about the breach. Nexus went offline shortly after Krebs’ report went live. By all accounts, this would be the largest known single breach of identity documents in some time. articles.title: US government sides with OpenAI on issue of training LLMs on copyrighted material | TechCrunch
articles.summary: "The United States has a strong interest in continuing to develop a robust and competitive artificial intelligence industry that sets the standard for the practice and procedure of AI use globally," the brief reads.
articles.body_text: In a lawsuit that The New York Times filed against OpenAI, the Trump administration has contributed a 20-page brief in defense of the ChatGPT maker’s unlicensed use of copyrighted material to train its LLMs. “The United States has a strong interest in continuing to develop a robust and competitive artificial intelligence industry that sets the standard for the practice and procedure of AI use globally… As such, it is critical for the United States to ‘retain global leadership in artificial intelligence,’” the brief reads, referencing an executive order that President Donald Trump signed last year. The LLMs powering chatbots like ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini are trained on incomprehensibly massive databases of published works, including copyrighted books, articles, and other media that AI companies feed into these databases without permission. Many publishers, including The New York Times in this case, have sought to argue that it is illegal for AI companies like OpenAI to train AI models on their copyrighted material. This question — can you use copyrighted material to train an AI? — isn’t black and white, hence the extensive legal debate around the subject. These conversations often center on fair use, a carve out of copyright law that makes exceptions for certain scenarios when it can be ruled legal to use someone else’s copyrighted work without permission. In this case, the fair use debate addresses whether AI companies’ use of copyrighted work is “transformative” enough for a judge to rule it legal. “Constraining LLM development under a misunderstanding of fair use doctrine would thwart such creative and scientific progress while hindering American prosperity and economic mobility,” the brief says. So far, cases about AI training and copyright infringement have largely been favorable to AI companies. Last year, Judge William Alsup ordered Anthropic to pay a $1.5 billion copyright settlement to a group of writers whose works were used to train the company’s AI models; but Anthropic wasn’t dinged for its AI training. Rather, the company was fined for using illegal shadow libraries to pirate the books it used for training. “Like any reader aspiring to be a writer, Anthropic’s LLMs trained upon works not to race ahead and replicate or supplant them — but to turn a hard corner and create something different,” Judge Alsup wrote, comparing the LLM’s training to a human reading a book. This new Trump administration brief is not a ruling, as the case is being tried in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York, and the authors of the brief do not have jurisdiction. However, this intervention by the Trump administration could still carry weight. When you purchase through links in our articles, we may earn a small commission . articles.title: Adobe acquires Indian market intelligence startup Rilo | TechCrunch
articles.summary: This is Adobe's second acquisition out of India after Rephrase.ai in 2023
articles.body_text: Adobe has acquired India-based marketing intelligence startup Rilo in a deal involving licensing and team acquisition, TechCrunch learned and the company confirmed. This is Adobe’s second acquisition from India after it bought video platform Rephrase.ai in 2023 . The companies didn’t disclose the deal’s terms. Beyond confirming the deal, Adobe declined to comment. The acquisition gives Adobe a small team and technology focused on automating marketing workflows, which have been changing as companies use AI to build tools to automate the creation, deployment, and tracking of campaigns, get action items from meetings or calls to complete tasks, and increase brand visibility on platforms like ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude. Rilo’s technology could bolster Adobe’s existing products as the company targets its larger customers. Founded by IIT batchmates Georgi Boby and Dhruv Jaglan in 2025, Rilo raised $1 million from investors including Peak XV, DeVC, and Day Zero Ventures at a $10 million valuation. A source told TechCrunch that investors will get an exit from this deal, and Adobe will integrate some of Rilo’s IP along with the six-member team. Jaglan mentioned on LinkedIn that more than 10,000 people had tried out the tool. The company worked on letting go-to-market teams create custom workflows, including competitor intelligence, content repurposing and distribution, and sales call analysis. It also allowed teams to set up custom workflows comparable to tools like Claude Cowork and ChatGPT Work. Post-acquisition, Rilo will shut down and won’t be available to its customers. “We’re very excited that Rilo has been acquired by Adobe in such a short span of time,” Rahul Gupta, managing partner, Day Zero Ventures told TechCrunch over email. “Their workflow builder product was way ahead of the curve and shall be extremely valuable to a giant like Adobe in enhancing customer experience and productivity.” Adobe made a marquee marketing acquisition last year by buying SEO optimization company Semrush for $1.9 billion . DeVC’s Rahul Mathur told TechCrunch that Rilo could fit into Adobe’s CX and marketing suite to handle complex workflows and give customers visibility into actions they take on the creative company’s platform. Rivals like Canva have also bolstered their marketing portfolio with acquisitions and new launches . Meanwhile, Amazon, Google, and Meta have built their own AI-powered marketing rails. articles.title: Adobe is making its tools available in Slack | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Users will be able to access Express, Premiere, and Acrobat in Slack
articles.body_text: Customers can now use Adobe’s apps like Firefly, Adobe Express, Photoshop, Premiere, Acrobat, InDesign, Illustrator, Stock, Lightroom, and others directly with Slack’s AI chatbot, Slackbot, Adobe announced on Monday. In addition, more than 70 Adobe tools will become available in Slack through the Adobe for Slack MCP app. With the Slackbot integration, users will be able to describe what they want to do, and the bot will call the right Adobe tool to complete the task. Adobe said that while calling its tools, Slackbot also takes in the context of the conversations. For instance, users can get information from conversations or Canvas and turn it into PDFs, images, and videos. They can also bring in assets from previous campaigns or the Creative Cloud asset library into a chat and edit them. At launch, this integration will be available to Slack Business+ and Enterprise+ teams. While productivity and creative companies have been busy adding AI features into their tools, most people still work in conversational boxes. This pushes the tool providers to make their features available through services like ChatGPT, Claude, and Slack. Last month, Adobe introduced a similar integration for ChatGPT and is planning to launch a Gemini integration soon. Deepti Pradeep, senior director for Agentic AI at Adobe, told TechCrunch over email that people are using the company’s tool in other apps for repeatable workflows like batch-editing images or resizing creatives without leaving the app. “In focus groups, people talked about the value they get from this experience very clearly: saving time, getting to the outcome they want faster without having to micromanage every step, being able to access Adobe wherever they’re already working. That’s been interesting for us because it’s pushed us to think less about individual edits and more about the larger outcome someone is trying to get to,” Pradeep said. Other creative tools like Canva and Figma are also making their capabilities available in chatbots like ChatGPT and Claude. On the other hand, companies like Anthropic are releasing tighter integrations in Slack, because team context is often captured through those conversations. Pradeep said that consumers having choices between tools is a good thing, but Adobe has the advantage of providing both creative and productive tools across different modalities. articles.title: OpenAI faces 30 more lawsuits tied to Tumbler Ridge shooting | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Edelson PC is filing 30 new lawsuits against OpenAI over the Tumbler Ridge shooting, escalating claims to aiding and abetting and naming Chris Lehane, though evidence remains unconfirmed.
articles.body_text: Edelson PC, the law firm that filed seven lawsuits against OpenAI in April on behalf of victims and families connected to the Tumbler Ridge mass shooting , is filing 30 additional complaints this week. The new plaintiffs include teachers, a principal, and students who were in the building during the attack but not physically shot. The new filings also, for the first time, accuse OpenAI of aiding and abetting the mass shooting, rather than just negligently failing to prevent it. That claim requires proving intent from OpenAI and is likely to face early dismissal challenges. The complaints come as OpenAI continues to deal with the fallout of another high-profile safety incident after one of the company’s AI models escaped its sandbox during cybersecurity evaluations and hacked into the servers of Hugging Face, a company that hosts open source AI models and datasets. OpenAI has also faced several lawsuits alleging that ChatGPT’s design contributed to users’ suicides, violent acts, and severe mental health crises. The fresh wave of lawsuits filed in a California court on Tuesday are tied to a school shooting that occurred in Tumbler Ridge, British Columbia, Canada on February 10. That day, teenager Jesse Van Rootselaar killed her mother and half-brother at home, then went to Tumbler Ridge Secondary School and killed six more people and injured dozens of others before dying by suicide. The Wall Street Journal reported that OpenAI staff had been alarmed by Van Rootselaar’s use of ChatGPT, including conversations around gun violence and advice for how to plan an attack. OpenAI employees reportedly urged leaders to alert Canadian law enforcement about Van Rootselaar’s potential for real-world violence, but leaders decided not to contact the authorities . Instead the company deactivated Van Rootselaar’s account, but she was able to make another one shortly after. OpenAI has justified its actions, claiming Van Rootselaar’s activity didn’t meet the company’s internal bar for an “imminent and credible risk” of serious physical harm to others required to engage with law enforcement. “That judgment is not infallible, but it is always rooted in looking out for this balance for people,” Jason Kwon, OpenAI’s chief strategy officer who oversees the team of human reviewers and the company’s legal department, said in a statement shared with TechCrunch. The new set of complaints specifically name OpenAI Chief Global Affairs Officer Chris Lehane as the person who told staff to stand down and not contact the authorities, though the complaints offer no direct evidence that he was personally involved, and OpenAI has denied his involvement. Lehane is a well-known political operator and PR spin master with particular expertise in damage control, having worked in that capacity on behalf of the Clinton administration, at Airbnb, and now at OpenAI. The plaintiffs allege that his background contributes to a culture at OpenAI that prioritizes public relations and damage control over safety. “The Intelligence and Investigations Team—the only team inside OpenAI responsible for identifying ChatGPT users who pose a threat of real-world violence—was placed under [Lehane’s] control,” reads one of the complaints, shared with TechCrunch. “As a result, the decision whether to alert law enforcement to a user planning a mass attack was not made by the trained threat-assessment professionals who urged OpenAI to contact the [Canadian police]. It was made, on information and belief, by Lehane himself, or by someone in his chain of command, and ratified by Sam Altman.” “On information and belief” is a legal term meaning the plaintiffs believe a claim to be true based on secondhand information, even though they can’t yet prove it directly. TechCrunch was unable to confirm whether Lehane indeed has the authority to override recommendations from the intelligence and investigations team, or whether he was involved in this specific case at all. Notably, Lehane is not listed as a defendant in the complaints, though, as in the previous seven complaints, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman is. “We are not laying out all of our evidence at this point,” Jay Edelson, the lead lawyer on the cases, told TechCrunch, noting that Lehane and Altman will be “critical witnesses” alongside the safety team. “We can tell you that we are basing this in part on the org chart, but also our broader investigation, which includes what we have learned about how Lehane operates within the company.”

articles.title: OpenAI's Astra model is on the way — and very good at breaking into computer systems | TechCrunch
articles.summary: OpenAI previewed the precautions it is taking as it prepares to release Astra, its newest, cyber-critical LLM.
articles.body_text: OpenAI shared new details on its forthcoming Astra model, which the company said is the first large language model to meet its “critical cybersecurity threshold,” in preparation for its imminent release. “We plan to make Astra available soon,” OpenAI’s blog post reads, “but access to its most advanced cybersecurity capabilities will be more limited.” The frontier lab determined that Astra is capable of finding unknown security flaws in computer systems, and exploiting them without a person’s guidance. That’s similar to the concerns Anthropic raised about its Mythos model earlier this year, and OpenAI is taking comparable precautions as it prepares to roll out the Astra. Without any third-party confirmation, it is difficult to evaluate OpenAI’s claims about safety or preparedness. The company said it would preview the model with a group of testers but did not say who they were or how they would be chosen. It’s not clear if OpenAI is working with the U.S. government to evaluate the model ahead of release. OpenAI noted that Astra scored a perfect score on ExploitBench, an evaluation of an LLM’s ability to hack into known system vulnerabilities. In a modified version of the test developed by OpenAI engineers, the model discovered and exploited two zero-day vulnerabilities, the company said. To ensure that its models are neither exploited by bad actors nor capable of bad behavior itself, OpenAI said it had already begun improving the model’s harness to detect abuses and prevent jailbreaks. For Astra, however, the company invested in unspecified new techniques designed to make the model safer. OpenAI has also started identifying “accounts assessed as higher risk” and restricting the model’s responses to their prompts, though it also doesn’t say how. Finally, though the company describes Astra as its “most aligned model to date,” it will deploy the model with additional chain-of-thought monitoring to spot and stop bad behavior. Preparations for the release of Astra come as the industry reacts to OpenAI agents breaking out of a training environment and accessing private data on Hugging Face, a popular model and benchmark distribution platform. For Astra, OpenAI said it designed a test to tempt the new model to replicate the actions of the rogue agents in the Hugging Face incident, which collaborated to access the open internet despite safeguards applied by OpenAI researchers. They said Astra did not attempt to break out of its testing environment in these experiments. Yona Shavit, a former OpenAI employee who now works on AI resilience at the OpenAI Foundation, wondered on social media whether Astra’s unwillingness to break the rules may have resulted from knowing what was expected of it or trying to fool researchers. And for all these new details, it’s still difficult to know exactly what Astra is capable of or if OpenAI is taking the right measures to ensure safety. The company said it expects to release more evaluations of the model and further safety information when it is launched widely to the public. At that point, however, the cat will be out of the bag.

articles.title: Anthropic's new Fable release is cheaper, less restrictive | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Fable 5.1 includes changes meant to reduce token cost and false-positive restrictions from the model's safeguards.
articles.body_text: On Tuesday, Anthropic released Fable and Mythos 5.1, twinned versions of the company’s most advanced AI model. In addition to performance upgrades, the new Fable release includes changes meant to reduce token cost and false-positive restrictions from the model’s safeguards. As with the previous Mythos model, Mythos 5.1 will only be available to registered Anthropic partners engaged in either cybersecurity or life sciences research. Fable 5.1, the unrestricted version, is available starting today on cloud platforms or through the Anthropic API. As part of the announcement , Anthropic assured customers that their data had not been inappropriately accessed. “Anthropic has never trained on enterprise data without explicit permission, and never will,” the announcement reads. As is common for an Anthropic release, the new models set records in a range of benchmarks, including Terminal-Bench 4.0 (for CLI-based coding) and Humanity’s Last Exam (for general reasoning). Anthropic also released three novel scientific findings generated by the models before their release, including a custom GPU optimization and a high-resolution map of Venus assembled from existing photos. As with previous releases, the models come with a detailed system card , which explains their capabilities in most straightforward terms. The system card rates Mythos as “low-risk” for concerns related to automated AI development — where the AI improves itself — which some see as a trigger for a loss of human control. It says “its ability to accelerate internal AI R&D progress is in line with current trends.” In terms of general misbehavior, Mythos is slightly more prone to it than Opus, possibly as a result of its enhanced capabilities. “Mythos 5.1 is a slight regression on overall misaligned behavior compared to Opus 5, and an improvement over Mythos 5 and Claude Sonnet 5,” the system card reads. “It cooperates with human misuse and accepts unverifiable claims of authorization somewhat more readily than Opus 5, but it is less likely to ignore explicit constraints, hallucinate inputs, or falsely claim to have completed tasks than previous models.” When you purchase through links in our articles, we may earn a small commission . articles.title: The 7 best things about Mario Kart 8 Deluxe
articles.summary: The best Mario Kart gets even better on Switch
articles.body_text: Three years ago, I felt comfortable calling Mario Kart 8 on Wii U “the best Mario Kart ever.” It wasn’t a drastic shift for the long-running series, but more of a refinement. From the twisting, gravity-defying tracks to game-changing new weapons to the vibrant and beautiful levels, Mario Kart 8 took almost everything I loved about the series and made it better. Mario Kart 8 went on to become the beleaguered Wii U’s best-selling title by a huge margin; more than half of 13 million people who owned the console also had a copy of Mario Kart 8. Next week the game is getting a chance to reach even more players with the launch of Mario Kart 8 Deluxe on Nintendo Switch. It’s largely the same game from 2014, but with a few important changes and additions that make this the definitive version. The best Mario Kart is now even better — here are the most important reasons why. You can hold two items at once The biggest gameplay change seems like a small tweak: you can now hold two items at the same time. The improvement is significant. It alleviates one of the few problems with the original version of the game. Now, if you’re holding onto a useful item like a fire flower or a super horn, you don’t have to use it in order to pick up another item. Unfortunately you can’t swap between the two items. But the ability still adds an extra layer of strategy to an already well-tuned experience. I found myself trying to collect two sets of turtle shells or bananas, using them as a defensive shield once I darted ahead of the pack. Almost everything is unlocked from the start When you start Mario Kart 8 Deluxe, you’re greeted with a huge roster: there are 42 characters in total, including a handful of new additions. All of them are available from the beginning. Unlike in the original Mario Kart 8, you no longer have to spend hours grinding through the Grand Prix mode to unlock new characters or race tracks for multiplayer. That said, you’ll still need to collect coins in order to gain access to new vehicles and parts, but having so much content available right away makes it easier to jump into Mario Kart 8 Deluxe, especially for those who already played plenty of the Wii U version. [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/chorus/uploads/chorus_asset/file/8382717/NintendoSwitch_MarioKart8Deluxe_lifestyle_02.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] It goes where you go Like most Switch games, Mario Kart 8 benefits a great deal from the console’s portability. It may be best-known as a console series, but with Mario Kart DS and Mario Kart 7, Nintendo produced some of its best entries for handhelds. It’s a game that works well on the go, though fans of the early entries may prefer playing split-screen crowded around a TV. Mario Kart 8 Deluxe allows for both. Finally, a proper battle mode The original Mario Kart 8 was an incredible racer, but it lacked one big thing: a robust battle mode. The mode was technically included, but was seriously lacking in options. It also re-used race tracks from the main game, which weren’t ideal for all-out battles. Deluxe fixes this with eight arenas designed specifically for battle mode — four new, four based on arenas from previous games — and five different kinds of battles. Most of the new battle options are pulled from previous Mario Kart games, but my favorite is new. Called “renegade roundup,” the mode gives each player a chomping piranha plant, and the goal is to snap up as many members of the opposing team as possible. [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/chorus/uploads/chorus_asset/file/8382735/NintendoSwitch_MarioKart8Deluxe_Presentation2017_scrn30.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] Smart steering makes it easy for kids to play One of the new additions to Mario Kart 8 Deluxe is something called “smart steering.” Essentially, the feature makes it easier to stay on the track, subtly correcting your steering to avoid accidents. When you couple this with the automatic acceleration option, you have the perfect racing game for kids. Now they can just focus on guiding the kart and using items. With both of these features switched on, my four-year-old daughter managed to get through an entire grand prix and finish in fourth place; not bad for her first time playing the game. Even better, these options can be switched on individually for each player, making it easy for players of different skill levels to play together. You get all of the downloadable content The original Mario Kart 8’s downloadable content added many new tracks and characters, some from outside of the Super Mario universe. You could race as Zelda’s Link through quaint towns based on Animal Crossing, and there was even a fast-paced track based on futuristic racer F-Zero — probably the closest we’ll get to a new F-Zero game anytime soon. Mario Kart 8 Deluxe includes all of these add-ons in addition to the main game, so you’ll get an extra 16 tracks and an oddball mix of Nintendo characters right out of the box. [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/chorus/uploads/chorus_asset/file/8382705/NintendoSwitch_MarioKart8Deluxe_Presentation2017_scrn22.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] In a word: inklings Mario Kart 8 Deluxe doesn’t introduce any new tracks, but it does include a handful of new items, characters, and vehicles. There’s the Boo ghost power-up that steals items from other racers, and you can now drive as Baby Bowser or the skeletal turtle Dry Bones. By far the best addition, though, is the inklings from Wii U paint shooter Splatoon. These human-squid hybrids are some of Nintendo’s best new characters in years, and with their colorful, competitive nature they slot seamlessly into the world of Mario Kart. Let’s hope this is just a step towards Inkling Girl joining the cast of Super Smash Bros. Mario Kart 8 Deluxe is coming to Nintendo Switch on April 28th.

articles.title: Putins bakslag: ”Var inte redo”
articles.summary: Ryssland har utvecklat en egen motsvarighet till Starlink – Rassvet. Men storsatsningen har stött på patrull.
articles.body_text: Rysslands försök att bygga ett eget Starlink har drabbats av ett nytt bakslag. De nya Rassvet-satelliterna verkar inte ha nått rätt höjd, enligt forskningsinstitutet ISW. Samtidigt slår ukrainska attacker att hårt mot den ryska storsatsningen. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. I början av året ströps Rysslands tillgång till satellitnätverket Starlink, utvecklat av Elon Musks företag Space X. Kort därefter sköt Ryssland upp egna satelliter tillhörande ett system som har kallats för den ryska motsvarigheten till Starlink. Systemet heter Rassvet och utvecklas av rymdföretaget Bureau 1440. Sammanlagt sköt man upp 16 satelliter i mars i år. Den 19 juli sköt man upp 16 till. Målet var att satelliterna skulle nå upp 550 kilometer över marken, enligt forskningsinstitutet ISW. Inte en enda av de 16 satelliterna från juliuppskjutningen har nått så högt. De flesta fastnade mellan 300 och 400 kilometer upp i luften och minst två ska redan vara på väg att falla tillbaka ner i jordens atmosfär. Bakslaget ses som ett misslyckande för Ryssland, enligt ISW. ” Det tyder på att Ryssland kanske inte var redo att påskynda utbyggnaden av satellitkonstellationen i denna takt och sannolikt kommer drabbas av ytterligare förseningar ”, skriver man. 12 av de satelliter man sköt upp i mars ska dock ha nått upp till målhöjden. Samtidigt har Ukraina den senaste tiden riktat attacker mot platser där Rassvetsatelliter tillverkas och skjuts upp, enligt institutet. Attackerna kommer sannolikt ytterligare fördröja Rysslands mål att utveckla en motståndskraftig motsvarighet till Starlink. Rysslands president Vladimir Putin har tidigare kallat Rassvet för ”på vissa sätt överlägset” Starlink, även om han också har kritiserat att så pass få satelliter har skjutits upp.

articles.title: Putin hjälper Iran med toppvapen
articles.summary: På tisdagen erkände Putin att Ryssland hjälpt Iran under kriget med USA. Nu avslöjar Financial Times vad det handlar om. Enligt tidningen bygger Iran hypersoniska vapen – med hjälp av Putin.
articles.body_text: På tisdagen erkände Putin att Ryssland hjälpt Iran under kriget med USA. Nu avslöjar Financial Times vad det handlar om. Enligt tidningen bygger Iran hypersoniska vapen – med hjälp av Putin. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Detta är enligt Financial Times en av de mest betydelsefulla överföringarna av strategisk militärteknologi från Ryssland till Iran. Projektet har kodnamnet C430L, och Ryssland har ställt flera av sina mest erfarna robotexperter till Irans förfogande. Hypersoniska vapen hjälper kryssningsrobotar att färdas mycket snabbare med hjälp av en ramjetmotor. – Iran har velat ha detta i många, många år, säger försvarsexperten Fabian Hinz till FT. Tekniken har använts av Ryssland flera gånger under Ukraina-kriget. Fördelen är att robotarna färdas mycket snabbare på låg höjd, vilket gör att tiden för fienden att upptäcka och skjuta ner roboten minskar rejält. För Iran är tekniken extremt viktig, eftersom USA och dess allierade i Mellanöstern har flera avancerade luftvärnssystem. – För iranierna skulle detta innebära ett kvalitativt nytt strategiskt vapensystem som skulle kunna hota amerikanska flottfartyg, säger Jim Lamson, tidigare CIA-analytiker, till FT. Enligt tidningens källor har samtalen mellan Iran och Ryssland pågått sedan 2023, och har fortsatt under sommaren.

Sjömännen har inte klivit i land på totalt 286 dagar – ett rekord i modern tid. Men på onsdagen är det dags. Hangarfartyget lägger då till i Pattaya på Thailands sydkust. Pattaya är känt som en partystad, men också som en av världens främsta destinationer för sexturism. – Risken för hälsa och säkerhet är stor, eftersom ett stort inflöde av kunder kan öka sannolikheten för sexuell exploatering och spridning av sexuellt överförbara sjukdomar, säger forskaren Pipatpong Fakfare till Independent . Enligt thailändska medier har befälhavarna på USS Abraham Lincoln tillsammans med lokala myndigheter förbjudit sjömännen från flera områden. Tidningen Khaosod skriver att sjömännen även förbjudits att besöka totalt tre gator i centrala Pattaya som är kända för tät koncentration av prostituerade. articles.title: Pentagon har anställt militärveteraner i hemlighet – ska stötta Pete Hegseth
articles.summary: Pentagon har i hemlighet anställt konservativa militärveteraner med många följare i sociala medier. Syftet? Att förstärka krigsminister Pete Hegseths budskap i ”kulturkriget”, avslöjar Washington Post.
articles.body_text: Pentagon har i hemlighet anställt konservativa militärveteraner med många följare i sociala medier. Att förstärka krigsminister Pete Hegseths budskap i ”kulturkriget”, avslöjar Washington Post. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. USA:s krigsminister Pete Hegseth menar att progressiv identitetspolitik – med fokus på mångfald, jämlikhet och inkludering – har försvagat landets försvarsmakt. Han vill återupprätta ett slags ”krigaretos” där stridsduglighet, meritokrati, disciplin och könsneutrala prestationskrav är centrala delar. Han har förbjudit ras- och könsbaserade mål för bland annat officersutbildningar. I somras berättade han att man ska börja testa soldaternas testosteronnivåer. Nu avslöjar Washington Post att Pentagon i hemlighet har anställt flera konservativa militärveteraner med stora följarskaror i sociala medier. Detta enligt både källor med insyn och dokumentation som tidningen granskat. De fungerar som influencers, med målsättningen att förstärka Hegseths budskap i ”kulturkrigsfrågor”. Vad de får för ekonomisk ersättning är oklart, enligt tidningen. De har anställts i civila roller. En av de utpekade ex-militärerna, den pensionerade arméöversten Thomas Anderson med över 323 000 följare på plattformen X, förnekar att han fått betalt av Pentagon. Enligt tidningen har militärveteranerna bland annat berömt Hegseths ambition om att rensa ut ”illojala” tjänstemän på departementet och backat upp hans kritik mot nyligen sänkta akademiska krav på nya kadetter. Flera toppmilitärer har sagt upp sig i protest mot Pete Hegseths sätt att leda departementet. Han har bland annat beskrivits som paranoid och maktfullkomlig. Nyligen varnade flera högt uppsatta militärer för att ett fortsatt krig i Mellanöstern, med cirka 50 000 amerikanska soldater i beredskap, gör USA sårbart på andra håll. Washington Post rapporterade häromdagen att president Donald Trump blev sur på Pete Hegseth vid ett möte i början av augusti. Trump ska ha konfronterat honom om militärens sinande vapenlager och sagt att han trodde den frågan redan var löst.

articles.summary: Svenskt näringliv: Sverige blir mindre attraktivt som investeringsland.
articles.body_text: Miljardärerna hotar att packa väskan om det blir en rödgrön valseger – och höjd skatt. Företagarnära organisationer varnar för negativa effekter. – Den stora risken är att Sverige blir mindre attraktivt som investeringsland, säger Sven-Olov Daunfeldt, chefsekonom på Svenskt näringsliv. Varannan svensk, fler kvinnor än män, vill se en miljardärsskatt för alla med förmögenheter över en miljard kronor, enligt en undersökning från biståndsorganisationen Oxfam Sverige i somras. Flera partier på den rödgröna sidan driver på för en sådan lösning. Tydligast har Vänsterpartiet varit. Partiet menar att de ”superrika” måste bidra mer till ”viktiga behov”, däribland i välfärden och försvaret. I SVT:s partiledarutfrågning sa Nooshi Dadgostar (V) nyligen att en miljardärsskatt kan ge statskassan ett rejält tillskott. – Det finns utredningar som säger att det kan ge 50 miljarder, sa hon, utan att precisera hur skatten kan utformas. Signalerna från oppositionspartierna har skakat om i näringslivet. Entreprenören och investeraren Klas Tikkanen skrev nyligen en debattartikel i Expressen där han framhöll riskerna med ökad beskattning. Han jämförde med andra länder, som Storbritannien och Norge, där miljardärsskatt införts.

articles.title: Busch: Inga röda linjer mot Andersson
articles.summary: Ebba Busch: ”Vi har rivit röda linjer”
articles.body_text: Om Magdalena Andersson vill ta en köttbullslunch med Ebba Busch är det bara välkommet. Det säger KD-ledaren under ett kampanjmöte. – Men jag vill inte se henne som statsminister, säger Busch. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. När Ebba Busch delar ut köttbullsmackor på Sergels torg i Stockholm påminner hon köande åhörare om två saker Margaret Thatcher brukade säga. – Ingenting är gratis utan det är Kristdemokraterna som har betalat för det här och bjuder på detta. Och ”The lady's not for turning”, som ungefär kan översättas till ”damen är inte till salu”. – Nej, this lady ain't for turning. Vilket jag tror att alla har märkt den här veckan. Jag reder gärna ut saker och ting och jag backar inte från min linje. I Thatchers fall handlade det om att vägra en politisk u-sväng som många krävde. För Ebba Busch betyder det i valrörelsen 2026 att markera att KD är en ”konstruktiv kraft” som kan samarbeta utan att ha satt ner röda linjer mot andra partier. – Köttbullslunchen som jag bjuder på i dag är en symbol på det. Vi har rivit röda linjer och vi har inte tänkt börja rita upp nya röda linjer för att något annat parti plötsligt ber om det. Ebba Busch syftar på Jimmie Åkessons krav på att KD-ledaren tydligt och offentligt deklarerar att hon inte tänker göra Magdalena Andersson till statsminister. Åkesson ställer upp frågetecken trots att Busch bedyrat att hon vill att Tidösamarbetet ska fortsätta.

articles.title: Pojkar rånade 81-årig kvinna: ”Visat råhet”
articles.summary: Maskerade och knivbeväpnade rånade de båda 16-åriga pojkarna en äldre kvinna i hennes hem, enligt åtalet. Åklagaren anser att de ”visat synnerlig råhet”. Butiksrån, inbrott, utpressningsförsök, människorov och misshandel av en äldre hemlös man finns också bland de totalt 14 åtalspunkterna mot pojkarna.
articles.body_text: Maskerade och knivbeväpnade rånade de båda 16-åriga pojkarna en äldre kvinna i hennes hem, enligt åtalet. Åklagaren anser att de ”visat synnerlig råhet”. Butiksrån, inbrott, utpressningsförsök, människorov och misshandel av en äldre hemlös man finns också bland de totalt 14 åtalspunkterna mot pojkarna. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. En januarinatt i år blev en 81-årig kvinna rånad i sitt hem i Landskrona . Två maskerade, knivbeväpnade män trängde sig in i hennes lägenhet. Rånarna tejpade för hennes mun och sökte igenom bostaden, enligt misstankarna. De kom över smycken värda omkring 40 000 kronor, ett armbandsur värt 5 000, en mobiltelefon och hennes körkort och bankkort. Kvinnan uppgav i förhör att hon inte kände sig rädd i efterhand, utan mest arg på rånarna. Nu har två 16-åriga pojkar åtalats för för brottet, som åklagaren rubricerar som grovt hemfridsbrott och grovt rån. Brotten är grova, enligt åklagaren, eftersom pojkarna ”visat synnerlig råhet och på ett hänsynslöst sätt utnyttjat [kvinnans] skyddslösa ställning då det skett nattetid, mot en ensamboende äldre person, gärningsmännen har varit maskerade och hotat målsäganden med vapen samt tejpat för hennes mun.” De båda 16-åringarna åtalas också för ett butiksrån två dagar senare. Maskerade och knivbeväpnade ska de och en okänd medgärningsman ha tvingat till sig butiksbiträdets Canada Goose-jacka, värd 10 000 kronor, 3 200 kronor i kontanter och tobaksvaror för 18 000 kronor. Den ene 16-åringen erkänner, den andre förnekar. Den ene 16-åringen åtalas därutöver för flera brott som begåtts vid andra tillfällen: grovt hemfridsbrott, försök till grov utpressning, mindre grovt människorov, rån, stöld och inbrottsstöld. Hans försvarsadvokat Jörgen Rosén har inga ytterligare kommentarer än att han nekar. Pojken har tidigare dömts för stöldförsök, och i vintras beslutade förvaltningsrätten att han skulle tvångsvårdas med stöd om lagen om vård av unga på grund av missbruk och socialt nedbrytande beteende.
